candidates.text:
Business workflow:
1. Sales order created. The sales order is created in the Sales module. Its open order deliveries are the base for the ASN.
2. Sales ASN created against the sales order. The user raises a new ASN (ASN For: Article or Kit), chooses the Buyer and adds the open order deliveries through the Select Order picker (S-1a).
3. ASN Type check. With GDN: the FG Allocation tab is shown by default and the normal ASN flow applies; no automatic stock transactions are raised. Without GDN: the setting decides (step 4).
4. Setting check, “FG Allocation without GDN”. ON: the FG Allocation tab is added to the ASN. OFF: no FG Allocation tab; the ASN works as a standard ASN and no stock transactions are raised.
5. FG allocation entry. In the FG Allocation tab the user enters the Site and the quantity to allocate (Trf. GDI Qty) on each row. Stock Type is Free, not linked to any OC.
6. Confirm sales ASN. The user confirms the ASN (V-2, V-3). The automatic transactions are controlled by the setting.
7. Automatic stock transactions. For each Site the system raises Enter New Stock, then Transfer Out of System, using the Site and quantity from the FG Allocation tab, in the same action as the Confirm.
8. Sales ASN confirmed. The ASN gets its Shipment No., becomes read-only, and the confirmation banner lists the stock transaction numbers.

chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Overview
chunks.text: Functional specification for the development team, generated from the finished New ASN mock screens in the Product Mock Studio (feature library wfx-erp-product-sales, menu Sales ▸ ASN). The mock is intentionally lenient; this specification is not — it is the contract the development team builds from. It contains ASSUMED answers pending product-team sign-off (see Open questions).
chunks.locator: § Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Overview

chunks.title: Purpose
chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Overview › Purpose
chunks.text: An Advance Shipment Notice (ASN) tells the system what is being shipped to a buyer: which open order deliveries, how many pieces, at what price, from which dispatch site, with which charges and shipping details. The New ASN screen lets the logistics team raise an ASN, save it as a draft, and confirm it. Confirming gives the ASN its Shipment No., locks it, and — for an ASN without a GDN — raises the two stock transactions that bring the finished goods into stock and send them out of the system. This lets the warehouse dispatch finished goods that are not yet held in system inventory, while keeping a full stock record against the ASN and its sales order.
chunks.locator: § Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Overview › Purpose

chunks.title: Who uses it
chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Overview › Who uses it
chunks.text:
• Logistics / shipping coordinators — raise, save and confirm ASNs.
• Inventory team — receive the automatic Enter New Stock and Transfer Out of System transactions.
• Finance and customs teams — read the confirmed ASN (values, charges, licence and shipping details).

chunks.title: Problem statement
chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Problem statement & proposed solution › Problem statement
chunks.text: Finished goods need to be dispatched from the warehouse against a sales order, but the stock is not available in the system's inventory. Without system stock a GDN-based dispatch cannot be made, so the shipment is either held or dispatched outside the system, and the stock and shipment records are lost.
chunks.locator: § Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Problem statement & proposed solution › Problem statement

chunks.title: Proposed solution
chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Problem statement & proposed solution › Proposed solution
chunks.text:
A new system setting, FG Allocation without GDN, enables a stock-less dispatch flow in the Sales ASN. When the setting is ON and the ASN Type is Without GDN, the FG Allocation tab is shown on the ASN. The user enters the Site and the stock quantity to allocate, with stock type Free (not linked to any OC). When the user confirms the sales ASN, the system automatically raises two transactions using the Site and quantity from the FG Allocation tab:
• Enter New Stock: brings the free stock into the selected Site.
• Transfer Out of System: moves the same stock out of the system against the ASN.
The goods are dispatched without existing inventory, with no manual stock entries, no leftover stock, and full traceability to the ASN and its sales order. The whole flow is switched on or off by the one setting.
chunks.locator: § Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Problem statement & proposed solution › Proposed solution

chunks.title: Business workflow
chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Problem statement & proposed solution › Business workflow
chunks.text:
Sales ASN workflow: FG allocation without GDN
• Sales order created. The sales order is created in the Sales module. Its open order deliveries are the base for the ASN.
• Sales ASN created against the sales order. The user raises a new ASN (ASN For: Article or Kit), chooses the Buyer and adds the open order deliveries through the Select Order picker (S-1a).
• ASN Type check. With GDN: the FG Allocation tab is shown by default and the normal ASN flow applies; no automatic stock transactions are raised. Without GDN: the setting decides (step 4).
• Setting check, “FG Allocation without GDN”. ON: the FG Allocation tab is added to the ASN. OFF: no FG Allocation tab; the ASN works as a standard ASN and no stock transactions are raised.
• FG allocation entry. In the FG Allocation tab the user enters the Site and the quantity to allocate (Trf. GDI Qty) on each row. Stock Type is Free, not linked to any OC.
• Confirm sales ASN. The user confirms the ASN (V-2, V-3). The automatic transactions are controlled by the setting.
• Automatic stock transactions. For each Site the system raises Enter New Stock, then Transfer Out of System, using the Site and quantity from the FG Allocation tab, in the same action as the Confirm.
• Sales ASN confirmed. The ASN gets its Shipment No., becomes read-only, and the confirmation banner lists the stock transaction numbers.

chunks.text:
• Toolbar: Export (Excel), Import (a stub — Q-4), Add, Delete (needs a ticked row; asks “Remove n order(s) from this ASN? Their shipment, FG allocation and style rows are removed too.”).

• Add needs the Buyer first (otherwise “Choose the Buyer before adding orders.”). It opens the picker with: Include Linked Buyers (checkbox), Dispatch Site (required), ETD (required) and Search.
• The picker lists the buyer’s order deliveries that: belong to the header buyer (or to a linked buyer when the checkbox is ticked); hold stock at the chosen Dispatch Site; have a Delivery Date on or before the ETD; and still have an open balance above 0 (ordered − already shipped).

GDI Qty entered here are the values the two automatic stock transactions use on Confirm; a note explains that the two stock transactions are raised on Confirm. chunks.title: Save, Confirm and Exit
chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › New ASN (S-1) › Save, Confirm and Exit
chunks.text:
• Save needs ASN For, ASN Type, ASN Against, Buyer, Invoice Type and Logistics Lead; otherwise the warning “Fill in: …” lists what is missing. A first Save stores the ASN as Saved and moves the address to /sales/asn/{id}; the page stays open and editable. Success: “The ASN was saved.”
• Confirm needs everything Save needs plus Invoice Date, Shipment Mode, Shipping Bill Date, Bill To, at least one order, a Price above 0 on every Shipment Details row, and a charge name on every charge row. A missing item shows “Fill in: …”. When all is present a dialog asks “Confirm this ASN? A confirmed ASN can no longer be edited.” On OK the ASN gets its Shipment No. (the next number after the highest in use, starting at 125001), becomes Confirmed and the page turns read-only.
• A Confirmed page is the same screen with every field and grid locked, the Save and Confirm buttons gone, and a green banner: “Shipment {no} is confirmed. This ASN can no longer be edited.” For Without GDN it adds the numbers of the stock transactions that were raised, or says none were raised because nothing was allocated or the setting is off.
• Exit returns to the ASN List (asking first when there are unsaved edits).
• The list row is refreshed on every Save and Confirm: Shipment No., Buyer, Style, Destination, Shipped Qty, Status.
Confirmed ASN — read-only, with the banner naming the two stock transactions

chunks.title: Automatic stock transactions on Confirm (ASN Type Without GDN)
chunks.heading: Sales ASN — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › New ASN (S-1) › Automatic stock transactions on Confirm (ASN Type Without GDN)
chunks.text:
• Raised only when ASN Type is Without GDN, the FG Allocation tab is shown (setting “FG Allocation without GDN” ON), and at least one allocation row has a Site and a Trf. GDI Qty above 0.
• For each Site two transactions are created, in this order: Enter New Stock (stock comes in at the site) and Transfer Out of System (the same quantity goes out against this ASN). Each carries the ASN’s Shipment No., the Site, the allocated lines (article, colour, size, UOM, quantity) and the total quantity. Site and quantities are populated from the FG Allocation tab; the user does not enter them again. Numbers run per type: ENS-000001, ENS-000002 … and TOS-000001 … (mock format; the real numbering is Q-3).
• The Confirm is one action: if the transactions cannot be stored, the ASN is not confirmed and “Could not confirm the ASN.” shows.
• With GDN, or with the setting OFF, or with nothing allocated, no transaction is raised.
